Connor / team / Claire — attaching a short procurement options matrix and a draft one‑page MOU for a 90‑day pilot. High level notes below:

Attachments:
- procurement_options_matrix.xlsx (breaks down PO vs card vs AWS Marketplace private offer, effort, timeline)
- redwood_trial_mou.pdf (one‑page pilot terms: 90 days, trial credits cap, data handling summary)

Quick guidance:
- Card: fastest to spin up (SaaS sign-up + card) — low friction, good for < $5k/mo pilots, but not preferred for enterprise procurement tracking.
- Direct PO / Invoice (Net30): Preferred by procurement. We can accept a PO for Redwood Hosted. Legal turnaround ~5–7 business days for standard terms if no redlines.
- AWS Marketplace Private Offer: preferred for long-term (easier for procurement to track spend and use existing AWS marketplace contracts). Private Offer setup adds ~2–4 weeks (legal + AWS listing admin), and AWS may require a private offer agreement. Billing flows through AWS; we can mirror pricing to direct PO but there are invoice timing differences.

KMS/SSO considerations (Karthik to confirm): Private Offers do not inherently change our KMS approach — KMS integration for Redwood Private remains customer-managed. If they buy via AWS Marketplace, enforcement of KMS/SSO is still under their VPC/on-prem config; the private offer only governs billing. If there are additional procurement clauses around key custody, we should surface them early.

Next steps proposed:
1) Claire: pick preferred pilot route (Card / PO / Marketplace Private Offer) — if PO, share billing contact and PO template; if Marketplace, we will start Private Offer intake and loop legal.
2) We will send the attached MOU and a 1‑page procurement summary to speed approvals.
3) 30‑min sync tomorrow 10am PT to align — Connor to send invite.

Ben
